The answer above is spot on.

To add a vivid example: the barbershop haircut recording that went viral online a few years ago sounds incredibly real on headphones. It was actually recorded with a dummy head (shaped like a human head, with a microphone fitted at the position of each ear), which mimics the human binaural hearing system. Our ears can tell where a sound is in space thanks to the differences in time and level between the signals arriving at the two ears, plus spectral cues that depend on the shape of the head, upper torso and outer ears.
